text:
Jordan Eberle is an original Kraken from the 2021 expansion draft, and at 36 he's still doing what he has done for years: a steady second wave of offense with a power-play job. Ten points in 15 games, six of them on the power play, and 783 career points before this season put 800 within reach this winter.

What's slipping is the five-on-five game around him. Seattle gets only 43% of the shot attempts and expected goals with Eberle on the ice, and he isn't a skater who can outrun that problem; his top speed sits near the bottom of the league. The good news is that his finishing hasn't run hot, so there's no luck to give back, and his own chance rate is in line with a 26-goal player, which is what he was last season. Our projection's middle case is about 53 more points, a full, useful season, if Seattle can tilt the ice a little more when he's out there. Pacific North Hockey called Seattle a "Perfect Fit For Eberle Family" this week, and it still looks that way.
headline: Still the steady second wave
